case_005:
angular_precise + deep_jewel confirmed (hard straight-cut lapel facets; forest-green/plum-maroon/navy at hue 213-262, v~0.12), but fine_tonal_hatching unreadable — face and neck are smooth gradients at 5x and the jewel-dark jacket hides any hatch strokes. -- overturned at full resolution: Thumbnail artifact — the hold does not survive full-resolution inspection.

RESOLUTION
case_005 is manifest sheet 005 (`review/manifest.json` -> sheets[4].case_aliases[0]), style_id `linework_coloring_angular_precise_deep_jewel_fine_tonal_hatching_controlled_rim_complete_line_color`, scorecard.csv rows 14-16: test_ids P7000013 (seed 1001), P7000014 (seed 2002), P7000015 (seed 3003). All three 1024x1024 renders inspected at 1:1 and at 3x-8x NEAREST crops, plus an unsharp/high-pass pass to expose low-contrast stroke texture in the dark garment.

WHAT FULL RES SHOWS
- angular_precise + deep_jewel: re-confirmed. Hard straight-cut lapel facets and crisp angular plane boundaries; plum-maroon / forest-green / near-black-navy garment at very low value.
- fine_tonal_hatching: READABLE in seed 2002 (P7000014). The navy left-shoulder/upper-chest jacket panel carries regular, evenly-spaced fine parallel diagonal hatch strokes — consistent angle, ~3-5 px pitch, textbook fine tonal hatching. They are visible at 1:1 in the un-enhanced render and unmistakable at 3x with no contrast boost at all. That is exactly the region the reviewer wrote off as "the jewel-dark jacket hides any hatch strokes": the strokes are 1-2 px wide sitting in a low-contrast dark field, so they are destroyed by the ~5x contact-sheet downscale. That is a resolution artifact, not a missing trait.

SEED DISAGREEMENT, AND WHY IT IS NOT THE DEFECT
Seeds 1001 and 3003 show no discrete hatch strokes — skin and garment shade as finely stepped tonal planes and smooth gradients (confirmed on 8x cheek/nose and neck crops and on the whole-image high-pass, which surfaces only plane-boundary edges and broad brush streaks). But this is the token's normal expression, not an item-level failure: the sibling item case_006 (`..._fine_tonal_hatching_reflected_color_...`, P7000016-18) is equally subtle across all three of its seeds. This is the same reasoning the brief attaches to airy_pastel saturation — a trait that renders faintly by design is only evidence of a defect when it falls below its own class's norm. case_005 sits at or above that norm; it is in fact the item that does produce visibly hatched strokes in a seed. Against the broad_blended_plane sibling case_001 (P7000001) at matched seed 1001, case_005's skin also reads as finer, subtler tonal stepping versus case_001's blockier broad plane facets, so distinctiveness on the shading factor is intact.

SATURATION SCREEN (checked for completeness; colour was never the concern)
tests/reports/phase7_linework_coloring_v2/saturation_screen.json: deep_jewel group median 0.1628, min 0.1107, max 0.2117 across 43 items, outlier_count 0; outlier_total 0 across all 300 items at deviation 0.5. No colour evidence against this item.

Verdict: the trait the reviewer could not read at thumbnail scale is present and legible at full resolution. holds=false.

case_245:
deep_jewel absent — all three seeds wear flat near-black tops (v 0.064-0.088, no discernible hue) whereas case_005 shows real jewel hue at comparable darkness; transparent_glaze therefore unreadable on that black mass, leaving only rounded_soft plausible. -- overturned at full resolution: case_245 = style_id linework_coloring_rounded_soft_deep_jewel_transparent_glaze_controlled_rim_complete_line_color, test_ids P7000733 (seed 1001), P7000734 (2002), P7000735 (3003). All three full-res renders inspected; seeds agree (plain crew-neck tee, near-black, on all three).

Both prongs of the hold reasoning fail at full resolution.

1) "deep_jewel absent / no discernible hue" — false. The garment is not achromatic. Mean garment RGB per seed is (18.6,16.4,15.9), (21.4,18.8,19.3), (22.5,19.4,20.1) — a consistent red/magenta-leaning dark, and under a level stretch (0-42 -> 0-255) the mass resolves as a uniform plum/aubergine (amethyst) wash on all three seeds, not multi-hue channel noise. Hue direction is stable across seeds, which noise would not be. Garment-region mean saturation is 0.1864 against a deep_jewel group median of 0.2003 — rank 18 of 43, mid-pack, with 18 accepted peers lower (e.g. rounded_soft_deep_jewel_crisp_shape_shadow 0.1624, crisp_uniform_deep_jewel_crisp_shape_shadow 0.2003 at v=0.0740, selective_edge_deep_jewel_broad_blended_plane 0.2118 at v=0.0692). On the whole-image metric the screen actually uses, my replication puts it at 0.1762 versus a deep_jewel median of 0.1664 — ABOVE its own group median. saturation_screen.json (deep_jewel: 43 items, median 0.1628, min 0.1107, deviation 0.5) reports outlier_count 0 and outlier_total 0 across all 300 items, so this item is not flagged by the discipline designed for exactly this concern. Near-black garments at v 0.07-0.09 are the norm for deep_jewel in this rig, not specific to case_245.

2) The cited comparator is misread. case_005 (P7000013) is not at "comparable darkness": its garment measures v=0.1130 versus 0.0816 here (~40% brighter), and its readable jewel hue comes from a multi-panel tailored jacket — dark burgundy lapel plus a dark green shirt — rather than from a comparably dark single mass. It is a garment-design difference, not evidence that this render lost its palette.

3) "transparent_glaze unreadable" — false. Compared against its five shading-mode siblings within rounded_soft + deep_jewel, transparent_glaze is the lowest-edge-energy and narrowest-range member (edge 1.54, tonal range 36, std 5.30) versus crisp_shape_shadow 3.42/68, broad_blended_plane 3.46/71, soft_two_band 3.65/67, fine_tonal_hatching 4.40/65, subtle_contact_shadow 2.55/51. Smooth translucent tonal build with no hard shadow boundary is precisely the glaze signature, and it separates cleanly from every sibling — so the factor is readable, and distinguishable, on that mass.

Residual caveat: at 100% zoom the tee does sit at the subtle end of deep_jewel, and the plum lean is perceptually less obvious than a blue lean at equal chroma, which is what made it read as flat black in the contact sheet. But subtlety at the low end of a group is not a defect under the stated rule, and the item is at or above its own group's median on the screen's metric. Thumbnail artifact.
